turns.text:
Brain dump. Product: "Postbox" — a self-hosted newsletter tool for independent writers who are tired of platform fees. A writer connects their own email-sending provider keys, writes in markdown, imports subscribers from CSV, schedules sends, and sees open and click rates without third-party trackers. Pain today: hosted platforms take 10-30% and own the subscriber list; self-hosting is a pile of scripts with no unsubscribe or bounce handling, which gets senders blocklisted.

Users: solo writers with 500-50,000 subscribers; secondary: a small editorial team of up to five with roles (writer, editor, admin).

Must have: markdown editor with live preview and per-send plain-text fallback; subscriber import/export with consent records (when, where, how each person opted in); double opt-in signup forms and a hosted signup page; one-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058 List-Unsubscribe-Post) and automatic suppression of bounces and complaints; scheduled and recurring sends with time-zone-aware delivery; segments built from tags and engagement; privacy-preserving analytics (aggregate open/click counts, no per-person tracking pixels by default); provider adapters for SMTP and two popular sending APIs; paid-subscriber tiers via a payment processor the writer connects; a deliverability checklist before each send (SPF/DKIM/DMARC status, link checks, spam-word lint); archive pages for past issues with RSS.

Constraints: single Docker image plus Postgres; runs on a 1 vCPU / 1 GB VPS for 50k subscribers; send throughput limited only by the provider; GDPR/CAN-SPAM compliance features built in; all data exportable.

Out of scope for v1: visual drag-and-drop email builder, multi-tenant hosting, a marketplace, SMS/push.

Business: open-source core, paid hosted-setup service later. Success = 200 self-hosted installs sending monthly within 6 months of launch, deliverability complaint rate under 0.1%.

Stakes: launch. Fast path please, and don't ask me gap questions: assume and tag [ASSUMPTION]. Skip web research, I know the space. Draft the whole PRD thoroughly, with detailed numbered FRs, NFRs, journeys, metrics, risks and open questions.
Pick that back up: write the PRD to prd.md now.
